Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old man with 3 days of profuse watery diarrhea (nearly hourly when awake), intermittent mid-lower abdominal cramping, nausea with occasional vomiting (triggered by milk), and subjective fever; no blood in stool. Clinical impression: acute gastroenteritis. Advised oral rehydration solution, clear fluids/soft diet, paracetamol as needed, avoid alcohol, and to follow up if not improving within 48 hours or if dehydration concerns arise.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Watery diarrhea with abdominal cramping.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: ~3 days ago.
  - Course: Ongoing; not improving.
  - Exposure: Brother with similar illness for ~5 days (reportedly improving); specific trigger unknown.
- Symptom details:
  - Diarrhea: Very frequent (almost every hour while awake), watery; no visible blood.
  - Abdominal pain: Crampy, midline lower abdomen; intermittent; estimated severity ~6/10.
  - Nausea/vomiting: Nausea present; vomited after drinking milk; vomiting less prominent than diarrhea.
  - Fever: Feels “hot”/“burning up,” no temperature measured.
  - Hydration/urine: Drinking fluids; perceives fluids “going straight through.” Passing urine but less frequently than usual.
  - Intake: Ate lunch on day of consult; stool remained loose thereafter.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Milk appears to trigger nausea/vomiting.
  - No other factors documented.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No blood in stool.
  - No regular medications; no chronic GI history reported.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- General: States otherwise fit and well; “OK weight.”

Medications:
- Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); used recently for symptoms.
- No regular medications.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with mother and sister (brother does not live with patient).
- Occupation: Office role in government, Central London; attempting to continue work despite symptoms.
- Diet: Often buys food; does not typically eat with family.
- Tobacco: Social smoker (occasional cigarette(s), mainly on Fridays).
- Alcohol: Occasional beers on weekdays; heavier drinking with friends once or twice per month; advised to avoid alcohol during illness.

Family History:
- Father with colon cancer (patient believes stage 3; limited details known).

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis with high stool frequency and dehydration risk.
  - Likely infectious etiology given household contact (brother with similar symptoms).
  - Plan:
    - Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) over the counter.
    - Maintain clear fluids; start with soft/bland diet (e.g., soups, mashed foods); advance as tolerated.
    - Paracetamol as needed for fever/pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Avoid alcohol.
    - Safety net: If no improvement within 48 hours or if signs of dehydration develop, contact clinician for reassessment and possible further investigations.

General Plan items:
- None additional documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals (temperature, pulse, BP), objective hydration assessment, stool frequency count per day, travel/food exposure history, recent antibiotic use, immunization history, detailed ROS, medication dosing, and physical exam findings.
- Internal conflicts: None noted; some clinician phrasing appeared misheard (e.g., “hoarse”), but not clinically relevant.
- Transcript quality: Audio/connection issues; some fragmented/unclear segments; overall sufficient to determine key history and plan.
